```plato
    //==
    // # Quad3D
    //
    // Measured through the A-B-C / A-C-D TRIANGULATION. Exact for the planar case
    // the declaration calls ideal; for a genuinely non-planar bilinear patch the
    // triangulated area UNDERSTATES the curved surface area (the two flat triangles
    // are the chordal approximation of it) and the centroid is that of the two
    // triangles rather than of the patch. TODO(content): the bilinear patch's own
    // area is an elliptic integral with no closed form; a quadrature helper would
    // be needed to do better.

    // The four vertices in stored order.
    Points(q: Quad3D): Array<Point3D>
        => [q.A, q.B, q.C, q.D];

    // The sum of the two triangles A-B-C and A-C-D.
    Area(q: Quad3D): Number
        => Triangle3D(q.A, q.B, q.C).Area + Triangle3D(q.A, q.C, q.D).Area;

    // The sum of the four side lengths.
    Perimeter(q: Quad3D): Number
        => q.Points.ChainLength(true);

    // The area-weighted mean of the two triangles' centroids, which is the exact
    // area centroid for a planar quad.
    Centroid(q: Quad3D): Point3D
    {
        var first = Triangle3D(q.A, q.B, q.C);
        var second = Triangle3D(q.A, q.C, q.D);
        var total = first.Area + second.Area;
        return first.Centroid.Lerp(second.Centroid, second.Area / total);
    }

    // The quad with all four vertices carried through the mapping.
    Deform(q: Quad3D, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): Quad3D
        => (mapping(q.A), mapping(q.B), mapping(q.C), mapping(q.D));

    //==
    // # Tetrahedron, wedge, and convex-volume bodies
    //
    // Volume, surface area, bounds, centroid and containment bodies for the flat-faced
    // solids declared in `spatial-primitives.types.plato`. `SignedVolume` and the scalar triple
    // product it is built from carry the sign convention the tetrahedron's declaration
    // states. The conventions governing every body here are in the shared section
    // above.

    //==
    // # Tetrahedron
    //
    // https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrahedron

    // The four vertices in stored order.
    Points(t: Tetrahedron): Array<Point3D>
        => [t.A, t.B, t.C, t.D];

    // Six times the signed volume of the simplex (a, b, c, d): the scalar triple
    // product (b - a) x (c - a) . (d - a). Positive when d lies on the side of
    // triangle (a, b, c) its right-hand-rule normal points to. The orientation
    // predicate the containment test below is built from.
    SixTimesSignedVolume(a: Point3D, b: Point3D, c: Point3D, d: Point3D): Number
        => a.Between(b).Cross(a.Between(c)).Dot(a.Between(d));

    // The signed volume, positive when D lies on the positive side of triangle
    // A, B, C — the sign convention the declaration states.
    SignedVolume(t: Tetrahedron): Number
        => SixTimesSignedVolume(t.A, t.B, t.C, t.D) / 6.0;

    // The magnitude of the signed volume; never negative.
    Volume(t: Tetrahedron): Number
        => t.SignedVolume.Abs;

    // The sum of the four face triangles.
    SurfaceArea(t: Tetrahedron): Number
        => Triangle3D(t.A, t.B, t.C).Area
        + Triangle3D(t.A, t.B, t.D).Area
        + Triangle3D(t.A, t.C, t.D).Area
        + Triangle3D(t.B, t.C, t.D).Area;

    // The arithmetic mean of the four vertices, which for a simplex is also its
    // volume centroid.
    Centroid(t: Tetrahedron): Point3D
        => ((t.A.X + t.B.X + t.C.X + t.D.X) * 0.25,
            (t.A.Y + t.B.Y + t.C.Y + t.D.Y) * 0.25,
            (t.A.Z + t.B.Z + t.C.Z + t.D.Z) * 0.25);

    // True when the four sub-tetrahedra formed by replacing one vertex with the
    // query all have the SAME orientation as the whole — equivalently, when all
    // four barycentric coordinates are non-negative. A zero term means the query is
    // on that face, so the boundary is included.
    Contains(t: Tetrahedron, point: Point3D): Boolean
    {
        var whole = SixTimesSignedVolume(t.A, t.B, t.C, t.D);
        return SixTimesSignedVolume(point, t.B, t.C, t.D) * whole >= 0.0
            && SixTimesSignedVolume(t.A, point, t.C, t.D) * whole >= 0.0
            && SixTimesSignedVolume(t.A, t.B, point, t.D) * whole >= 0.0
            && SixTimesSignedVolume(t.A, t.B, t.C, point) * whole >= 0.0;
    }

    // The tetrahedron with all four vertices carried through the mapping.
    Deform(t: Tetrahedron, mapping: Function1<Point3D, Point3D>): Tetrahedron
        => (mapping(t.A), mapping(t.B), mapping(t.C), mapping(t.D));

    //==
    // # Wedge
    //
    // A triangular prism: the Base triangle swept by Offset, possibly obliquely.

    // |(AB x AC) . Offset| / 2 — the base area times the component of Offset
    // perpendicular to the base. Correct for an oblique sweep (Cavalieri).
    Volume(w: Wedge): Number
        => w.Base.TwiceVectorArea.Dot(w.Offset).Abs * 0.5;

    // The two triangular ends plus one parallelogram per base edge, each of area
    // |edge x Offset|.
    SurfaceArea(w: Wedge): Number
        => 2.0 * w.Base.Area
        + w.Base.A.Between(w.Base.B).Cross(w.Offset).Magnitude
        + w.Base.B.Between(w.Base.C).Cross(w.Offset).Magnitude
        + w.Base.C.Between(w.Base.A).Cross(w.Offset).Magnitude;

    // The base centroid displaced by half the sweep; the wedge is uniform along
    // Offset.
    Centroid(w: Wedge): Point3D
        => w.Base.Centroid + w.Offset * 0.5;

    // The union of the base triangle's bounds and the swept copy's.
    Bounds(w: Wedge): Bounds3D
        => UnionOfBounds(w.Base.Bounds, w.Base.Bounds.TranslateBounds(w.Offset));

    // True when the query solves (point - A) = u*AB + v*AC + s*Offset with u, v
    // and u+v in [0, 1] (inside the base triangle) and s in [0, 1] (inside the
    // sweep). Solved by Cramer's rule on the 3x3 frame; each determinant is a
    // scalar triple product. Boundary inclusive. Undefined (division by zero) when
    // Offset lies in the base plane. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cramer%27s_rule
    Contains(w: Wedge, point: Point3D): Boolean
    {
        var ab = w.Base.A.Between(w.Base.B);
        var ac = w.Base.A.Between(w.Base.C);
        var ap = w.Base.A.Between(point);
        var determinant = ab.Cross(ac).Dot(w.Offset);
        var u = ap.Cross(ac).Dot(w.Offset) / determinant;
        var v = ab.Cross(ap).Dot(w.Offset) / determinant;
        var s = ab.Cross(ac).Dot(ap) / determinant;
        return u >= 0.0 && v >= 0.0 && u + v <= 1.0 && s >= 0.0 && s <= 1.0;
    }

    //==
    // # ConvexVolume

    // True when the query is behind EVERY bounding plane (the normals point
    // outward), which is exactly the intersection of the half-spaces. Boundary
    // inclusive. An empty plane list reports true — the intersection of no
    // half-spaces is all of space.
    Contains(v: ConvexVolume, point: Point3D): Boolean
        => v.Planes.All(p => p.SignedDistance(point) <= 0.0);
```
